name: ci

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:

jobs:
  smoke:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20
      - name: Syntax-check every .cjs / .js
        run: |
          shopt -s globstar nullglob
          for f in **/*.cjs **/*.js; do
            case "$f" in node_modules/*) continue;; esac
            node --check "$f"
          done
      - name: Install (no secrets required)
        run: npm install --no-audit --no-fund || true
      - name: Test (runs against the zero-dependency echo path)
        run: npm test

🐛 Bugbot

Two-stage code review for diffs — a finder proposes bugs, an adversarial refuter kills the false positives, and only survivors reach you.
Bugbot reviews unified diffs, not whole repos. A FINDER model traces data flow and error paths across the changed hunks and proposes candidate findings under strict noise rules (no style, no nits — only logic bugs, leaks, races, broken error handling, security, and contract breaks). Every candidate then faces a REFUTER: a second adversarial pass whose default verdict is KILL and which must fail to disprove a finding before it surfaces. Findings arrive as structured JSON — file, line, severity, failure scenario, suggested fix — and the CLI exits nonzero only on confirmed criticals, so it drops straight into CI. Models are one-function adapters; a built-in echo model runs the whole pipeline with no API key.

--- ## Why Bugbot Most LLM code review fails in one of two ways: it floods you with style nits, or it hallucinates bugs that a guard three lines up already prevents. Bugbot attacks both. Noise rules are baked into every prompt — style, formatting, naming, and taste are explicitly banned; only demonstrable defect classes are allowed. And no finding reaches you on the finder's word alone: an adversarial refuter re-examines each candidate against the same diff and context, assuming it is a false positive, hunting for the guard, the early return, the type narrowing, or the unreachable path that invalidates it. Its default verdict is kill. What survives is short, concrete, and worth your time — each finding names the file and line, the failure scenario with concrete inputs, and a minimal fix. Pipe any diff in, wire any model through a one-function adapter, and gate CI on the exit code. --- ## What it does | Module | What it does | Signal | |---|---|---| | **finder** | Traces data flow + error paths across changed hunks; proposes structured candidate findings under hard noise rules | bug classes only, never style | | **refuter** | Adversarial second pass per candidate — default verdict KILL; must fail to disprove a finding before it surfaces | false-positive firewall | | **normalizer** | Defensive JSON extraction (balanced-brace scan, fence stripping, one retry), severity/line coercion, actionability filter | malformed output never crashes a review | | **CLI + log** | stdin / --staged / --diff <ref> / --files a,b; exit 1 only on confirmed criticals; every run appends to data/findings.jsonl | drops straight into CI | --- ## Architecture ```mermaid flowchart TD D["unified diff\n(stdin / --staged / --diff ref)"] --> F["FINDER\ntrace data flow + error paths"] F --> C["candidate findings\n(structured JSON)"] C --> R{"REFUTER\ndefault verdict: KILL"} R -->|cannot disprove| S["confirmed findings\nfile · line · severity · scenario · fix"] R -->|refuted| K["killed\n(logged with kill reason)"] S --> E{"any critical?"} E -->|yes| X1["exit 1"] E -->|no| X0["exit 0"] classDef acc fill:#3d1f18,stroke:#E0654C,color:#fff; class R acc; class S acc; ``` --- ## Quickstart ```bash # 1. review your working-tree changes ($0 out of the box — built-in echo model) git diff | node lib/bugbot.cjs # 2. review what's staged (pre-commit style) node lib/bugbot.cjs --staged # 3. review the last commit, or specific files node lib/bugbot.cjs --diff HEAD~1 node lib/bugbot.cjs --files src/router.js,src/auth.js # 4. watch the full find → refute → survive pipeline on a canned buggy diff node examples/demo.cjs # 5. wire a real model (one function) and gate CI on the exit code BUGBOT_MODEL=./examples/model-adapter.cjs git diff origin/main | node lib/bugbot.cjs ``` > Out of the box Bugbot uses a deterministic built-in echo model that returns a clean review — so the pipeline, parsing, and CI gate all run with no API key. Point BUGBOT_MODEL at a module exporting async call(system, prompt) to review with a real model. Every run appends a JSONL record (files, candidates, confirmed, killed, timings) to ./data/findings.jsonl. --- ## See it run

--- ## Repository layout ``` bugbot/ ├── lib/ │ ├── bugbot.cjs ← reviewDiff() + reviewFiles() + the CLI; finder → refuter pipeline │ └── model.cjs ← resolves your BUGBOT_MODEL adapter, or the built-in echo model ├── examples/ │ ├── demo.cjs ← canned buggy diff + scripted model: one finding survives, one gets killed │ └── model-adapter.cjs ← a copyable real-model adapter template (async call(system, prompt)) └── data/ ← findings.jsonl run log (gitignored, auto-created) ``` --- ## Concepts | Concept | Meaning | |---|---| | **Finder** | The first model pass: traces data flow and error paths across the changed hunks and proposes structured candidate findings. | | **Refuter** | The adversarial second pass. It assumes every candidate is a false positive and hunts for the guard, early return, or unreachable path that kills it. Default verdict: kill. | | **Noise rules** | A prompt-level contract banning style, formatting, naming, and taste — only demonstrable defect classes are allowed to surface. | | **Candidate vs confirmed** | A candidate is what the finder proposes; confirmed is what survives refutation. Only confirmed findings are shown. | | **Kill reason** | Every killed candidate is logged with the refuter's concrete reasoning — auditable, never silently dropped. | | **CI gate** | The CLI exits 1 only when a confirmed critical survives — pipe a diff in and let the exit code decide the build. | | **Model adapter** | One async function call(system, prompt) wired via BUGBOT_MODEL; the built-in echo model runs the pipeline with no API key. | --- ## Design principles 1. **Diff-scoped, always.** Review the changed hunks plus provided context — never invent findings outside the diff. 2. **Noise is banned by contract.** Style, formatting, naming, and taste are excluded in the prompt itself; only demonstrable defect classes surface. 3. **Guilty until proven — for findings.** The refuter's default verdict is KILL; a finding must survive concrete refutation to reach you. 4. **Fail-soft, CI-native.** Model outages and malformed JSON degrade to an empty review; exit 1 fires only on a confirmed critical. ---

# Bugbot — Architecture

Bugbot reviews unified diffs, not whole repos. A FINDER model traces data flow and error paths across the changed hunks and proposes candidate findings under strict noise rules (no style, no nits — only logic bugs, leaks, races, broken error handling, security, and contract breaks). Every candidate then faces a REFUTER: a second adversarial pass whose default verdict is KILL and which must fail to disprove a finding before it surfaces. Findings arrive as structured JSON — file, line, severity, failure scenario, suggested fix — and the CLI exits nonzero only on confirmed criticals, so it drops straight into CI. Models are one-function adapters; a built-in echo model runs the whole pipeline with no API key.

## Flow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    D["unified diff\n(stdin / --staged / --diff ref)"] --> F["FINDER\ntrace data flow + error paths"]
    F --> C["candidate findings\n(structured JSON)"]
    C --> R{"REFUTER\ndefault verdict: KILL"}
    R -->|cannot disprove| S["confirmed findings\nfile · line · severity · scenario · fix"]
    R -->|refuted| K["killed\n(logged with kill reason)"]
    S --> E{"any critical?"}
    E -->|yes| X1["exit 1"]
    E -->|no| X0["exit 0"]
    classDef acc fill:#3d1f18,stroke:#E0654C,color:#fff;
    class R acc;
    class S acc;
```

## How it fits together

Bugbot is a two-stage agentic pipeline over a single injectable model function. `reviewDiff(diff, opts)` builds a finder prompt from the capped diff (512KB guard), optional surrounding context, optional known-failure-mode rules, and a hard noise contract, then asks the model for AT MOST N findings as a JSON array. Parsing is defensive by design: code fences are stripped, a balanced-brace scanner extracts the first valid JSON payload from up to eight plausible start points, and one self-correcting retry fires if the reply is unparseable. Candidates are normalized (severity coerced to critical/major/minor, line coerced to a positive integer) and filtered for actionability (file + summary + failure scenario required). Each survivor then faces the refuter sequentially — one model channel at a time — with a prompt that presumes the finding false and demands concrete code reasoning to confirm. Kills are kept with their reasons; confirms surface. `reviewFiles(root, files)` shells `git diff` (falling back to --cached) scoped to the file list and feeds the same pipeline. The model layer (`lib/model.cjs`) resolves a BUGBOT_MODEL adapter exporting `async call(system, prompt)` or falls back to a built-in deterministic echo model, so the entire pipeline — prompts, parsing, refutation, logging, exit codes — runs with no API key. Every run appends a structured record to ./data/findings.jsonl, and nothing in the pipeline throws to the caller.

## Extending it

Every capability is a self-contained module. To add your own, follow the contract the existing
modules use and wire it into the entry point. Keep it portable — config via `.env`, no hardcoded
paths, no personal accounts.

## Design principles

1. **Diff-scoped, always.** Review the changed hunks plus provided context — never invent findings outside the diff.
2. **Noise is banned by contract.** Style, formatting, naming, and taste are excluded in the prompt itself; only demonstrable defect classes surface.
3. **Guilty until proven — for findings.** The refuter's default verdict is KILL; a finding must survive concrete refutation to reach you.
4. **Fail-soft, CI-native.** Model outages and malformed JSON degrade to an empty review; exit 1 fires only on a confirmed critical.

what it does

Guilty until proven — for findings.

01 / FIND

Diff-scoped, noise-banned

The finder reviews only the changed hunks plus the context you pass. Style, formatting, naming, and subjective taste are banned by prompt contract; what remains is logic bugs, null derefs, races, resource leaks, swallowed errors, injection, and contract breaks — each as structured JSON with a concrete failure scenario.

02 / REFUTE

Every finding gets prosecuted

A second adversarial pass assumes each candidate is a false positive and hunts the diff for the guard or unreachable path that kills it. Confirm is only returned when refutation fails with concrete code reasoning. Killed candidates are logged with their kill reason — auditable, never silently dropped.

03 / GATE

An exit code CI can trust

Confirmed findings print human-readable with file:line, scenario, and a minimal suggested fix; the process exits 1 only when a confirmed critical survives. Pipe git diff in locally, or run --staged as a pre-commit hook. The whole run is fail-soft — a model outage degrades to a clean empty review, never a crash.

quickstart

Up and running in a clone.

Every value comes from .env. Nothing here is tied to any account — bring your own.

# 1. review your working-tree changes ($0 out of the box — built-in echo model)
git diff | node lib/bugbot.cjs

# 2. review what's staged (pre-commit style)
node lib/bugbot.cjs --staged

# 3. review the last commit, or specific files
node lib/bugbot.cjs --diff HEAD~1
node lib/bugbot.cjs --files src/router.js,src/auth.js

# 4. watch the full find → refute → survive pipeline on a canned buggy diff
node examples/demo.cjs

# 5. wire a real model (one function) and gate CI on the exit code
BUGBOT_MODEL=./examples/model-adapter.cjs git diff origin/main | node lib/bugbot.cjs
